items.prompt: A spinner produces one of the integers 1 through 8, with all eight outcomes equally likely. What is the probability that the result is at least 6?

In a fictional model, every manufactured part either needs rework or does not need rework. The probability that a randomly selected part needs rework is 0.27. What is the probability that it does not?

In a fictional group of 60 learners, 30 joined a drawing club, 24 joined a coding club, and 12 joined both. A learner is selected uniformly at random from the 60. What is the probability that they joined at least one of the two clubs?

A fictional log contains 100 builds: 30 ran on Windows and 70 on Linux. Of the Windows builds, 6 failed; of the Linux builds, 4 failed. A build is selected uniformly at random from the log. Given that it ran on Windows, what is the probability that it failed?

A fictional delivery list has 240 parcels. Exactly 60 were priority parcels. Of the 30 parcels that arrived late, 18 were priority parcels. A parcel is selected uniformly at random from this list. Given that it arrived late, what is the probability that it was a priority parcel?

A bag contains 3 red tokens and 2 blue tokens. Two tokens are drawn uniformly at random, one at a time, without replacement. Given that the first token was red, what is the probability that the second token is red?
A fully specified probability model gives P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.5, and P(A and B) = 0.2. Are the two events independent in this model, and which calculation establishes your answer?
options: No: 0.2 is smaller than either event's probability.
Yes: 0.4 and 0.5 add to a number below 1.

items.prompt: Events A and B are mutually exclusive: they cannot occur together. Their probabilities are P(A) = 0.3 and P(B) = 0.2. Are they independent?
options: Yes: never occurring together means observing either tells us nothing.
No: if B occurs, A has probability 0 instead of its original 0.3.
Yes: adding 0.3 and 0.2 gives 0.5, which is a valid probability.
No: every pair of different events must change each other's probability.

items.prompt: In a fictional system model, module A fails during a run with probability 0.10 and module B fails with probability 0.20. The two failure events are explicitly assumed independent. What is the probability that at least one module fails during a run?

In a fictional supply model, workshop A makes 60% of the sensors and workshop B makes 40%. A sensor from A is defective with probability 2%; one from B is defective with probability 6%. A sensor is selected at random from the combined supply. Given that it is defective, what is the probability it came from B?

In a fictional collection, 1% of files are defective. A checker flags 90% of defective files and also flags 10% of nondefective files. A file is selected uniformly at random. Given that the checker flags it, what is the probability that it is defective?

A fictional checker flags 90% of defective files and 10% of nondefective files. Compare two collections where the defective share is 1% and 10%, respectively. The checker's conditional flagging rates stay the same. How does P(defective given flagged) change as the defective share rises?
options: It stays at 9/10 in both collections.
It stays at 1/10 in both collections.
